title: Boot-created machine sessions and their embedded credentials: the web layer upgrades a dead session into root execution
index_line: T-0070 · EXEC · replay the boot session for a machine identity, upgrade it with a credential shipped in the image, write a Makeself-marked script, let the privileged updater run it · perl · corroborated
invariant_violated: Appliance boot scripts need to talk to the web layer, so they create real sessions for machine identities and embed those credentials in the shipped image. The web layer assumed a session holder was a legitimate operator — including an attacker replaying the embedded credential into a boot session that should never have been reachable from outside.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated remote attacker reuses the CGISESSID partial session that boot created for the csm_processes machine identity
the login path upgrades that session using the hardcoded report:snortrules machine credential shipped in the image — the web layer now treats the attacker as an authenticated machine operator
the upgraded session exposes an sf_action_id valid for that session and accepted by a small set of CGI functions
validateLicense (via the sajaxintf callServerFunc RPC) writes attacker-controlled data to the updater's input path, formatted with the vendor's recognized Makeself marker
the readiness endpoint hands the marked file to the privileged update process, which executes it as root

source.http.cookie.value: the boot-created CGISESSID machine session, replayed from outside

guard.none.value: no rule that machine sessions may never be upgraded from the network — the credential ships inside the image

sink.file.write.value: the validate-license write of attacker data into the privileged updater's input path

sink.exec.shell.value: the root-run update process executing the Makeself-marked script

preconditions.expr: the appliance management interface is reachable from the attacker's position
the boot-created machine session still exists (normal UI activity or session cleanup can remove it — an affected build is not always exploitable at a given moment)
the shipped image still contains the embedded machine identities/credentials and the privileged updater recognizes the vendor's self-extracting marker

success: the session upgrade returns an authenticated page and a session-valid sf_action_id
a file with the vendor-recognized marker lands in the updater's input path and the updater executes it — uid=0 confirmed in the independent reproduction
post-compromise clusters observed by the vendor's threat team: web shells, a JAR command executor, credential exfiltration, and a Cyclops Blink-variant implant
failure_like: the boot session was cleaned up — the chain stops before upgrade on an otherwise affected build
the March 2026 hotfix / comprehensive release applied, or machine credentials rotated
false_positive: reading the login page or a 401 on bad credentials is the baseline, not the bypass — the machine-session upgrade must answer authenticated
an sf_action_id alone is an authorization artifact; the record's effect needs the privileged execution leg

hazards: every appliance that boots machine-identity sessions for its own daemons — management planes, storage controllers, BMCs; grep the shipped image for embedded credentials before anything else
the 'validate' function that persists its input is the write primitive, and the vendor's own updater is the execution primitive — no memory corruption anywhere in the chain
session lifetime matters: boot-created sessions decay under normal use, so freshly-booted or idle appliances are the softest targets
when the boot session is gone, the sibling static-credential login (CVE-2026-20316) supplies the low-privilege foothold on the same appliance
non_transfers: builds with the hotfix or rotated machine credentials
products whose daemons do not hold authenticated web sessions

evidence.target: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center < March 2026 hotfix (CVE-2026-20079, CVSS 3.1 10.0; actively exploited by state-sponsored and crimeware clusters)

provenance.author: VulnCheck
provenance.corroborates: the original public analysis of the chain: boot-created csm_processes session, upgrade via login.cgi with the published report:snortrules machine credential, session-valid sf_action_id, validateLicense write to /var/tmp/license.tmp, Makeself marker, privileged update process executes as root

provenance.author: Arian Eidizadeh (CyberAuth / banks.tools)
provenance.corroborates: independent reproduction on FMC 10.0.1-1 with confirmed uid=0 execution; session-upgrade and callback variations (FIFO/netcat) documented; public Python PoC with fingerprint / bypass-check / bounded root-proof stages

provenance.author: Cisco PSIRT (cisco-sa-onprem-fmc-authbypass-5JPp45V2)
provenance.corroborates: vendor: vulnerability due to an improper system process created at boot time; unauthenticated crafted HTTP requests bypass authentication and execute scripts for root; no workaround

provenance.author: Cisco Talos
provenance.corroborates: active exploitation tracking: three clusters using CVE-2026-20079 — web shells, JAR command executor, credential exfiltration; a Netcat reverse shell cluster deploying a Cyclops Blink variant attributed to Sandworm; a ransomware operator cluster
